title: Head of Performance
description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

 

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision https://www.monumental.co/our-vision/ and company https://www.monumental.co/about/. About the role

We're hiring our first Head of People & Performance to own how we attract, develop, and stretch our team as Monumental grows from around 100 people to several hundred over the next few years. You'll work as an extension of the founders - your job will be to get the most out of everyone and scale the judgment our team currently have in their own heads. It is integral to us that we maintain a startup culture that does not dilute as we enter our next phase of growth.

You'll own the people side of how Monumental performs: who we hire, how we develop them, how we run our performance and equity cycles, and how we keep the bar high as the company grows. Our day-to-day people operations are already covered, so your job sits one layer above that, working directly with the founders and the leadership team.

This is a hands-on, operator role. Like everyone at Monumental, you'll pick up the projects with the biggest priority at any given moment - the special projects that often span several teams and don't yet have an owner. One month that might mean standing up our performance and equity cycles; the next it might mean scoping how a new function should be staffed, reading where a team is overstretched, or untangling a problem that doesn't belong to anyone yet.

The loudest internal conversations at Monumental are about how to do better work, and you'll help keep them there. You reach for direct contact and local knowledge over standardized process, and you distrust schemes that try to make people legible by flattening them.

You should be obsessed with talent. You care more about whether a junior engineer is being stretched than whether the handbook is up to date. You can sit down with anyone in the company - software, workshop, ops - and walk away knowing what they're building and what's blocking them.

What you’ll do

- Special projects: Like everyone at Monumental, you pick up the work with the biggest priority, wherever it happens to sit. Some of these are squarely people problems and many aren't. Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air & Missile Defense Radar team develops cutting-edge tracking algorithms and software systems that detect, track, and characterize airborne threats in real-time. Working in small, focused teams, our software engineers design and implement sophisticated tracking solutions that protect lives and critical assets. Our work spans the full spectrum-from developing novel multi-target tracking algorithms to building high-performance distributed systems that process massive amounts of sensor data in milliseconds

We don't just publish papers; we deploy production-grade systems that our government and industry customers depend on for mission-critical operations. If you're passionate about applying mathematics, software engineering, and signal processing to solve complex real-world problems, we want to hear from you.

Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. Tailscale is building the new Internet by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. We’re seeking a motivated Support Engineer (Tier 1) to join our growing team of support professionals. You will serve as the face of the company for a large portion of our community, handling a broad range of tickets that will help flex your technical muscles.

As a Tier 1 engineer, you’ll be part of a distributed team focused on delivering excellent support and proactively solving friction by partnering with our broader CX team and Product/Eng. This role reports directly to the Tier 1 Support Team Lead and will play a key role in our journey.

• Display a natural tinkerer’s mindset and a deep curiosity for how things work, likely demonstrated through personal projects, homelabs, or open-source contributions.

• Demonstrate a foundational understanding of networking fundamentals, including DNS, IP addressing, firewalls, and routing.

• Show proficiency in troubleshooting across multiple operating systems such as macOS, Windows, Linux, and mobile OS’s.

Essa pessoa será responsável por construir uma visão integrada dos riscos financeiros, apoiar a definição de limites e indicadores e atuar de forma próxima às áreas de Tesouraria, Finanças, Crédito, Contabilidade, FP&A e demais áreas relacionadas.

A posição atuará como segunda linha de gestão de riscos, avaliando e desafiando de forma independente as exposições, metodologias, limites e respostas conduzidas pelas áreas responsáveis pela operação. 

Buscamos um profissional com senioridade, autonomia e capacidade de transformar análises financeiras em recomendações práticas para a tomada de decisão. Não é necessário possuir o mesmo nível de profundidade em todos os tipos de riscos financeiros, mas é esperado conhecimento sólido em pelo menos uma ou duas dessas frentes, visão abrangente dos demais temas e disposição para desenvolver novas competências. 

Principais responsabilidades

• Apoiar a estruturação da metodologia, da governança e do roadmap de riscos financeiros da companhia.

• Identificar, avaliar e monitorar exposições relacionadas a:

• risco de liquidez (concentração, caixa, etc);

• risco de crédito e contraparte;

• risco de mercado (cambial, taxa de juros, inflação, etc);

• gerenciamento de capital;

• instrumentos financeiros e operações de tesouraria.

• Desenvolver indicadores-chave de risco - KRIs -, limites de exposição, gatilhos de alerta e mecanismos de escalonamento.

• Desenvolver, validar, e implementar metodologias quantitativas para gerenciamento de riscos financeiros, incluindo análises de cenários, testes de estresse, VaR (Value-at-Risk) e avaliações de sensibilidade.

• Monitorar a suficiência de liquidez e a capacidade financeira da companhia em diferentes cenários.

• Avaliar riscos associados a bancos, instituições financeiras, parceiros de pagamento e demais contrapartes.

• Acompanhar eventos, desvios de limites, perdas financeiras e planos de mitigação.

• Elaborar materiais executivos para a liderança, Comitê de Riscos, Comitê de Auditoria e demais fóruns de governança.

Everpure is seeking a full-time Embedded Firmware Simulation Engineer to join our device firmware team. You will be responsible for developing high-fidelity virtual platforms that abstract complex hardware behaviors to accelerate SSD firmware development. In this role, you will be responsible for:

• Developing and maintaining comprehensive firmware simulation environments (e.g., QEMU) to enable shift-left testing, reducing dependency on physical hardware and accelerating time-to-market.

• Creating accurate, high-fidelity hardware models to abstract controller logic, communication interfaces (PCIe, NVMe), and NAND media behaviors within Pure Storage’s DirectFlash™ SSD Modules.

• Designing and implementing instrumentation tools to profile performance and analyze failures within the simulated environment.

• Partnering closely with ASIC vendors to validate firmware behaviors against RTL and digital logic designs before physical silicon is available.

• 5+ years of experience building and scaling high-fidelity simulation software for complex embedded, firmware, or hardware-software systems.

• Expert-level proficiency in C/C++ and Python for both firmware and modeling development.

• Extensive experience with simulation/emulation tools and methodologies (e.g., QEMU, SystemC, TLM, or instruction-set simulators).

• Deep understanding of firmware-hardware interaction, including the ability to translate complex schematics and data sheets into abstract software models.

• Strong knowledge of high-performance storage protocols such as PCIe and NVMe.

• Experience with embedded software development, SoC bring-up, and RTOS.
